page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose, 6th-generation instance powered by 64 physical cores and 128 virtual cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, relying on EBS block storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results reveal top-tier multi-threaded processing power, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 191273.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 99308.37, both ranking in the top 10 percent. Cached memory read bandwidth reaches 9076.97 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput in-memory key-value operations such as Redis SET commands at 129.17 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU tasks and LLM text generation speeds remain within the average tier, indicating that execution performance favors distributed parallel execution over raw single-thread speed.

With its high core density and balanced memory allocation, the instance delivers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy multi-core applications that do not require dedicated local NVMe drives or specialized accelerator hardware. It is suitable for highly concurrent enterprise backends, large-scale Redis in-memory databases, software build farms, and high-volume web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 128 vCPUs (64 physical cores) driven by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor at 3.6 GHz and 512 GB of DDR4 memory on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Built with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it provides 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without local disk storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core CPU capacity and cached memory bandwidth, achieving over 129 million Redis SET operations per second and strong performance in multi-threaded workloads. While single-threaded performance ranks in the average tier, the hardware offers effective cost efficiency for parallel scale-up workloads by maximizing resource density on standard x86_64 architecture. This server is best suited for enterprise web serving, distributed caching, software compilation, and data processing.
